## Introduction

We will store two versions of `HealthWellbeing` in a local *pins*
board. The first contains all 29 studies. The second contains the 18
general-population studies, so we can explore how that restriction
changes the analysis. Both use the variable definitions from the data
dictionary, and both trace back to the same raw file.
[Dataset documentation](04_data_documentation.qmd)

Work from the project root with *box* and *pins* available and `health`
loaded from the verified snapshot. Use a fresh board for the writing
exercise. If you have already completed it, use your saved versions CSV
to repeat the retrieval. The instructor can provide a prepared local
board and its selection files if you need to catch up.

## Create a versioned board

We enable versioning so the board retains both writes. We use RDS, an
R format that preserves the column types. The board lives inside our
local workshop outputs.

```{r health-pins-setup, cache = FALSE}
box::use(
  pins[board_folder, pin_exists, pin_meta, pin_read, pin_versions,
       pin_write],
  utils[read.csv, write.csv]
)

workshop_dir <- file.path("outputs", "health-wellbeing")
data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
pin_name <- "health_wellbeing"
versions_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv")
selection_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "analysis-data-version.txt")
```

## Write and describe two versions

We record the raw checksum, source, and scope within each pin's
metadata. The first write keeps the supplied table as loaded.

```{r health-pins-write-full, cache = FALSE}
stopifnot(!pin_exists(data_board, pin_name), nrow(health) == 29L)

source_url <- paste0(
  "https://www.protectlab.org/meta-analysis-in-r/data/",
  "healthwellbeing.rda"
)
raw_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(
  file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
))
stopifnot(identical(raw_md5, "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"))

pin_write(
  data_board,
  health,
  name = pin_name,
  type = "rds",
  title = "HealthWellbeing",
  description = "All 29 studies in the teaching snapshot.",
  metadata = list(source_url = source_url, raw_md5 = raw_md5, scope = "all")
)
full_version <- pin_versions(data_board, pin_name)$version
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L)
```

The alternative input changes which studies are included. The metadata
records the filter and the parent version, so we can account for the
11 excluded studies. This is a teaching comparison based on study
population. The published example uses the full set.

```{r health-pins-write-general, cache = FALSE}
health_general <- health |>
  subset(population == "general population")
stopifnot(nrow(health_general) == 18L)

pin_write(
  data_board,
  health_general,
  name = pin_name,
  type = "rds",
  title = "HealthWellbeing",
  description = "Only studies labelled general population.",
  metadata = list(
    source_url = source_url,
    raw_md5 = raw_md5,
    scope = "general",
    filter = "population == 'general population'",
    parent_version = full_version
  )
)

history <- pin_versions(data_board, pin_name)
general_version <- setdiff(history$version, full_version)
stopifnot(length(general_version) == 1L)
history

versions <- data.frame(
  scope = c("all", "general"),
  version = c(full_version, general_version)
)
write.csv(versions, versions_file, row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(full_version, selection_file)
```

## Try it yourself

Retrieve the full dataset by its recorded identifier and inspect
its source metadata. The selection file tells the pipeline which
version to use when we start the next activity.

```{r health-pins-read-version, cache = FALSE}
versions <- read.csv(versions_file, colClasses = "character")
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L)

health_full <- pin_read(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version)
pin_meta(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version)$user
nrow(health_full)
```

## Checkpoint {#pins-checkpoint}

The history contains two versions with distinct identifiers. The saved
selection points to the full dataset and the retrieval returns 29
rows. Locate the identifier of the 18-study subset in
`dataset-versions.csv`. The version identifies a stored object within
this board. If you recreate the board elsewhere, use its new
identifiers and retain the upstream checksum and filter.

Keep the board local and share the source and transformation
instructions when reuse terms are unclear. Next we will make the
selection file a tracked pipeline input.
[Reproducible analytical pipelines](06_targets.qmd)
